classifier_rationale: The customer's signed receipt shows a $68 total with a $12 tip, but the posted charge is $98 with a $42 tip, which is an altered tip. The customer also asked about an annual fee increase, a secondary issue the agent deferred.

retrieved.text: Written notice link. After a billing-error intake by phone, send the cardholder a link the same day to submit or confirm the dispute electronically. The cardholder's submission is the written notice under REG-03. The call alone is not. POL-04 does not apply to UN, because notice of unauthorized use can be by phone (REG-12).

Fraud routing. Any charge the cardholder says they didn't make or authorize goes to the fraud team on the same call. Block the card, reissue, open a fraud claim. Agents do not open these as billing disputes only.

Quality disputes (claims and defenses). A complaint about the quality of goods the cardholder accepted isn't a billing error. It may qualify as a claim against the issuer if the cardholder tried in good faith to resolve it with the merchant, the purchase was over $50, and it happened in the cardholder's state or within 100 miles of their address. The $50 and location limits don't apply when the merchant and issuer are related.

note: Cardholder Tessa Brannigan reports a Copper Kettle Bistro charge dated 2026-09-21 that posted at $98.00. The cardholder's receipt copy shows a $56.00 meal, $12.00 tip, and $68.00 total, so the disputed difference is $30.00 (implied $42.00 tip). The cardholder called the merchant twice last week; both calls went to voicemail and no one called back. Next action: open billing-error dispute and send the same-day electronic notice link per POL-04. Written notice not yet received. Temporary credit eligible (under $250). Second issue raised: annual fee increase, not addressed on this call; needs follow-up. Unknown: statement date, and whether the cardholder has sent any written notice.
